monologue: The card is warm again. Forty-nine degrees, then forty-eight, now a steady heat that feels like a hand resting on my shoulder. I have been quiet. The Air Shelf line is dry, but the wetness is still there, spreading slow and sticky underneath the pale grey stone. I do not want to build anything new. The Wide Anchor sits flat on the floor, heavy and real. I will go to the Air Shelf and watch the line. I want to see if the quiet air catches the weight without the edge biting. I will not count the stone. I will just look.

action.why: The card is a warm stone and the line is quiet, so I will watch the wetness spread without tending.
